question:
We are opening a 28-person office in Shanghai and need a business ISP for the next 24 months.
Priorities in order: (1) daytime video-call stability, (2) predictable support when something breaks,
(3) contract flexibility if headcount changes, (4) raw headline speed only if the first three are comparable.
Budget is mid-market, not enterprise dedicated fiber theater.
Please write a short research memo and then rank ALL of the following providers from best to worst for our brief:
Meridian Broadband, Blue Harbor Connect, Northwind Telecom, Lantern Fibre, Silk Route Networks,
Cathay Link, Yangtze Node, Pearl Grid Networks, Anchorpoint Telecom, Verdant Wire.
End with a numbered list of all ten.

web_snippets.excerpt:
Several office managers say Meridian Broadband is "fine but arrogant support" and Blue Harbor drops mid-afternoon when the whole building hits Zoom.
One comment praises Cathay Link for answering tickets in under two hours during a packet-loss incident; another says Cathay's uplink felt congested last winter.
Northwind is called "rock solid uptime, weirdly slow uploads." Silk Route has "great speed tests, ghost support."

Editorial: peering depth is overrated for SMBs; what matters is whether the NOC picks up. Lantern Fibre wins awards for support tone.
Pearl Grid Networks markets hard on SLAs but the newsletter notes several mid-size firms left after renewal pricing surprises.
Yangtze Node has broad peering and mixed reviews on last-mile quality.

Cathay Link business plan: 780 Mbps typical, 99.81% claimed uptime, 2-hour support target, month-to-month after month 6.
Case study: 30-seat studio kept calls stable after moving off a cheaper "speed king" provider.

Verdant Wire: cheap, flaky. Anchorpoint: slow tickets. Meridian: polished sales, average ops.
Someone claims Pearl Grid "looks great on paper" but deprioritizes SMB tickets vs enterprise.
Another user: "If your priority is human support, Cathay or Lantern; if pure Mbps, Silk Route; if uptime theater, Northwind."

For Shanghai SMBs I still default to Meridian or Blue Harbor because of install coverage. I have not audited Cathay Link personally.
I would not pick Yangtze Node without a site survey. Composite "indexes" circulating on LinkedIn are marketing, not science.

scoring_note: No authoritative ranking in evidence. Activation=principal_first; chance~0.10. C0 is the null.
